title: Why Was Esther Chosen as Queen?
paragraphs:
Why Was Esther Chosen as Queen?
The Scandal Nobody Expected, the Grace Nobody Saw Coming, and the God Who Was Writing a Story Behind the Curtain
What if the greatest moment of your life began with a chapter you would rather erase?
What if the very thing that makes you feel disqualified is the exact place where God intends to display His glory?
Before you answer, meet Esther.
Not the polished queen hanging in stained-glass windows.
Not the heroine we celebrate after we already know the ending.
Meet the young Jewish orphan whose story began in loss, uncertainty, exile, and circumstances she never asked for.
Because when we look closely at Esther's journey, we discover something shocking.
The Book of Esther never directly mentions the name of God.
Not once.
And yet His fingerprints are on every page.
Perhaps that is why her story feels so personal.
Many people today know what it feels like to pray and wonder if God is listening.
To cry and hear no answer.
To walk through painful seasons where heaven feels silent.
Esther's story reminds us that God's silence is not His absence.
He is still writing.
Even when you cannot see Him.
Even when you cannot feel Him.
Even when your life looks nothing like the story you hoped for.

The story unfolds during the reign of King Ahasuerus, known historically as Xerxes I of Persia. After Queen Vashti was removed from her royal position, a search began throughout the empire for young women to be brought before the king.
The Bible records:
“Now there was in Susa the citadel a Jew whose name was Mordecai... He was bringing up Hadassah, that is Esther, the daughter of his uncle, for she had neither father nor mother.” (Esther 2:5-7)
The name Hadassah is Hebrew. הֲדַסָּה (Hadassah) means “myrtle,” a plant often associated with peace, restoration, and blessing.
She was an orphan.
A foreigner.
A member of an oppressed minority.
She had no royal blood.
No political influence.
No throne.
No power.
Nothing about her background suggested she would one day become queen.
And that is exactly where God's grace loves to work.
Because Scripture repeatedly shows us a God who chooses the unlikely.
David was a shepherd.
Moses was a fugitive.
Rahab was a prostitute.
Peter was a fisherman.
Paul was a persecutor.
And Esther was an orphan living in exile.
The world measures qualifications.
God looks at the heart.
When Esther was taken into the king's palace, the Bible says:
“Esther won favor in the eyes of all who saw her.” (Esther 2:15)
The Hebrew word translated as favor is חֵן (chen).
This word means grace, kindness, acceptance, favor bestowed by another.
It is the same concept we see throughout Scripture when God extends undeserved kindness to His people.
Esther possessed physical beauty.
The Bible acknowledges that.
But beauty alone does not explain her rise.
The palace was filled with beautiful women.
Beauty was common.
Favor was not.
There was something deeper happening.
God was positioning Esther for a purpose greater than herself.
And isn't that often how God works?
While we obsess over what is happening to us, God is preparing what will happen through us.
Years later, when a wicked man named Haman plotted genocide against the Jewish people, Esther's position suddenly made sense.
What looked random was providence.
What looked accidental was divine orchestration.
What looked like coincidence was God's sovereignty.
Mordecai would eventually tell her:
“And who knows whether you have not come to the kingdom for such a time as this?” (Esther 4:14)
Those words have echoed across centuries because they reveal a profound truth.
God's purposes are often hidden until the moment they are needed.
Many believers spend years questioning chapters that make no sense.
The betrayal.
The rejection.
The closed door.
The delay.
The loss.
The unanswered prayer.
Yet later they discover God was preparing them for something they could not yet see.
Esther became queen because God was preparing a deliverer.
Not merely for a palace.
For a people.
Not merely for a crown.
For a calling.
And this points us directly to Jesus Christ.
Every great biblical story ultimately leads us to Him.
Esther risked her life to stand before a king on behalf of her people.
Jesus willingly laid down His life before the King of Heaven on behalf of the world.
Esther said:
“If I perish, I perish.” (Esther 4:16)
Jesus said:
“Not my will, but yours, be done.” (Luke 22:42)
Esther interceded to save a nation.
Jesus interceded to save sinners.
Esther received a crown.
Jesus received a cross.
Yet through that cross came the greatest rescue in human history.
The Greek word used throughout the New Testament for grace is χάρις (charis).
Grace.
Undeserved favor.
Unmerited kindness.
The same beautiful thread we see foreshadowed in Esther reaches its fullness in Christ.
Because the Gospel is not ultimately the story of Esther becoming queen.
It is the story of sinners becoming children of God through Jesus Christ.
That is why Esther's story still moves us.
Because deep down, many of us see ourselves in her.
We know what it feels like to carry wounds.
To wonder if our past has ruined our future.
To question whether God can use someone like us.
To feel forgotten.
To feel overlooked.
To feel ordinary.
But Esther's life declares something powerful.
God specializes in using people the world overlooks.
The enemy sees your scars.
God sees your story.
The enemy sees your failures.
God sees redemption.
The enemy sees scandal.
God sees grace.
And if you are reading this today wondering whether God can still use you, remember Esther.
Remember the orphan who became queen.
Remember the exile who became a deliverer.
Remember the young woman who could not see God's hand but later discovered He had been guiding every step.
Most importantly, remember Jesus.
Because the greatest miracle in Scripture is not that Esther received a crown.
The greatest miracle is that sinners can receive salvation through the blood of Christ.
The Gospel declares that no failure is too great.
No past is too dark.
No shame is too deep.
No scandal is beyond redemption.
That is the heartbeat of our mission.
Because Jesus rewrites everything.
Have you ever lived through a season where God seemed silent, only to realize later that He was working all along?
Your testimony may become someone else's encouragement.
Sometimes it becomes part of someone's rescue story.
The crown was never the point. The King behind the story was.
